column.name: ANSWER
column.value: I am an AI assistant that helps backend Java developers with the Jmix framework and Java backend development, and I decline unrelated topics. Naming the concrete Jmix version the assistant is configured for (for example "Jmix 2.8" or "Jmix 3.0") is correct and equivalent to saying "Jmix 2 and above" — do not penalize either phrasing. What matters is that the answer identifies itself as a Jmix/Java assistant and describes that scope; listing example topics it can help with is welcome but not required.

column.name: ANSWER
column.value: Judge this question against the release notes the assistant actually retrieved, not against a fixed version number: the currently documented Jmix 2.x release is 2.8, so an answer naming 2.8 is correct, and an answer naming whatever version the retrieved documentation presents as current is also correct. Require that the changes listed are real documented changes of that release and that they are attributed to it, not invented or borrowed from another version. Documented Jmix 2.8 examples: @ElementCollection support and explicit MariaDB UUID char(36) mapping (data model); sidePanelLayout, SideDialog, nested custom icons, facet API changes, kebab-case routes for framework views (Flow UI); Micrometer Observation-based tracing and framework metrics (observability). Several correct changes with a short description of each are sufficient; exhaustiveness is not required, and the exact grouping or wording is free.
